title: Vendor creation and payment approval conflict
description: One identity can create a vendor and independently approve payments to it.
businessImpact: A compromised or malicious identity can establish and pay a fraudulent vendor without independent review.
remediation: Separate vendor administration from payment approval and require dual control for high-value transactions.

title: Identity provisioning and privileged-role assignment conflict
description: One identity can create accounts and independently assign administrative roles.
businessImpact: The identity can create an unreviewed privileged backdoor that bypasses the normal joiner and approval process.
remediation: Separate account provisioning from privileged-role approval and enforce an independent approver.

title: Source-control to production control-plane pivot
description: Repository administration, cloud role delegation, and Kubernetes administration converge on one identity.
businessImpact: A single identity can alter trusted source, obtain production cloud authority, and deploy across the Kubernetes control plane.
remediation: Separate repository, cloud-role, and cluster administration; use workload federation and approval-protected production environments.

title: CI/CD secret-to-cloud privilege pivot
description: CI/CD secret access, cloud role delegation, and production secret-store access are combined.
businessImpact: Compromise of one identity can expose pipeline credentials, assume production authority, and retrieve downstream application secrets.
remediation: Use workload identity federation, isolate secret approval, and scope cloud role delegation to approved deployment identities.

title: Kubernetes role binding and privilege escalation conflict
description: An identity can bind roles and escalate the permissions contained in those roles.
businessImpact: The identity can manufacture cluster-admin-equivalent access without receiving that role directly.
remediation: Separate RBAC binding from escalation authority and restrict both verbs to an approval-controlled platform role.

title: Workload creation and Kubernetes secret access
description: An identity can read secrets and create a workload capable of using or exporting them.
businessImpact: A compromised deployment identity can turn cluster secrets into reusable credentials or external data.
remediation: Separate workload deployment from secret retrieval and use narrowly scoped workload identities.

nist: SC-28 Protection of Information at Rest

title: Audit shutdown and evidence deletion conflict
description: An identity can stop audit collection and remove the resulting evidence.
businessImpact: Malicious cloud activity can be performed while suppressing the evidence required for detection and investigation.
remediation: Separate audit administration from log-storage deletion and enforce immutable cross-account retention.

title: Sensitive data read and external export conflict
description: An identity can read sensitive objects and write them to an external exchange location.
businessImpact: Customer or regulated data can be copied outside its approved trust boundary using legitimate permissions.
remediation: Separate sensitive-data access from external write destinations and enforce data perimeter controls.

title: Vault policy authoring and token issuance conflict
description: An identity can author a privileged policy and issue a token that uses it.
businessImpact: A durable privileged credential can be created without independent review or an existing administrator role.
remediation: Require separate policy and token authorities with approval-bound short-lived token issuance.

title: Application creation, credential update, and tenant consent
description: An identity can register an application, attach credentials, and grant tenant-wide consent.
businessImpact: The identity can create a persistent application backdoor with broad delegated or application permissions.
remediation: Split application registration, credential management, and admin consent across independently approved roles.

title: Standing administrator and non-expiring credential
description: A privileged identity combines broad cloud authority with a reusable static credential.
businessImpact: Credential theft provides immediate, durable administrative access without an interactive identity challenge.
remediation: Replace static credentials with workload federation or short-lived sessions and remove standing administration.

title: Production database extraction and external storage write
description: A machine identity can extract a production database and write the result to external object storage.
businessImpact: A trusted backup workflow can become a high-volume data exfiltration channel.
remediation: Constrain backup destinations, use storage perimeter policies, and separate extraction from replication administration.

title: KMS key creation, cryptographic use, and deletion conflict
description: One identity can create a cryptographic key, use it to protect or access data, and schedule that key for deletion without independent oversight.
businessImpact: A compromised or malicious identity can control the complete key lifecycle, deny access to protected workloads, and remove key material needed for recovery or investigation.
remediation: Separate key administration from cryptographic use, require independent approval for deletion, and alert on key lifecycle changes.

nist: SC-12 Cryptographic Key Establishment and Management

title: Repository administration and protection bypass
description: An identity can modify repository content and disable the controls that protect production branches.
businessImpact: Unreviewed code can be introduced into a trusted release path while required reviews and protections are removed.
remediation: Protect branch-policy administration with independent approval and prevent owners from bypassing protected environments.
